decisive_step: Manufacturing and assembly of the batting tee components in Canada
flip: If a non-originating specialized component (e.g., tee topper or shaft) classified in heading 9506 was imported into Canada and assembled, it would fail the shift from any other chapter and require analysis under 102.11(b).
reasoning: A baseball/softball batting tee is classified under subheading 9506.99, HTSUS. Under 19 CFR 102.20(s), the rule for 9506.40-9506.99 requires a change from any other chapter, or from subheading 9506.11-9506.39. Assuming raw materials (plastics of Ch. 39, rubber of Ch. 40, or metals of Ch. 72-83) are formed and assembled into the batting tee in Canada (consistent with the USMCA request context and precedent rulings like N352810), all foreign materials undergo the required tariff shift under 19 CFR 102.11(a)(3).
